SA05:A:band: The band and its canonical decompositions [Proved under the stated Tate hypothesis; the group calculation is unconditional]. Put \[ \Gamma=W(p)=\{\lambda\in\overline\Q^{\times}:\ p^N\lambda\text{ is integral for some }N\geq0, \quad |\tau\lambda|=p^{w(\lambda)/2}\ (\tau),\quad w(\lambda)\in\Z\}. \] Then $G=D(\Gamma)$, where $D$ is the contravariant equivalence from Galois modules to groups of multiplicative type. Let $\mu_\infty$ be the group of roots of unity, $\Gamma^0=\ker(w)$, and $M=\Gamma^0/\mu_\infty$. There are canonical identifications \begin{align*} X^*(G^0)&=\Gamma/\mu_\infty=M\oplus\Z[\sqrt p],\\ G/G^0&=\widehat\Z,\qquad G^0=H^0\times\Gm, \qquad H^0=D(M),\\ X^*(H)&=\Gamma'=\Gamma/\langle\mu_\infty,p\rangle =M\oplus\Z/2\Z,\\ H&=H^0\times\mu_2. \end{align*} The maps $\epsilon:G\to\Gm$ and $i:\Gm\to G$ have character maps $1\mapsto p$ and $\lambda\mapsto w(\lambda)$, respectively, and $\epsilon i(t)=t^2$. The restriction $i|_{\mu_2}$ splits $H$. The group $M$ is a $\Q$-vector space, and complex conjugation acts as $-1$. Consequently $H^0$ is a protorus, an inverse limit of tori compact at the real place. It is not an algebraic torus of finite type.

SA05:A:P: Geometric base change and the universal Frobenius [Proved under the stated Tate hypothesis; identification of character modules unconditional]. There is a canonical isomorphism \[ \Gamma/\mu_\infty\xrightarrow{\sim} W(p^\infty):=\varinjlim_{n\mid n'} \bigl(W(p^n),\lambda\mapsto\lambda^{n'/n}\bigr). \] Thus $G^0=P$, the Weil-number protorus of Langlands--Rapoport and Milne, and $H^0=P_0$, its weight-zero factor. The base-change functor $\mathcal M_p\to\mathcal M_{\overline{\F}_p}$ induces the inclusion $P\hookrightarrow G$ on bands. The inclusion $\Gamma\hookrightarrow\overline\Q^\times$ is Galois equivariant and hence defines a canonical $\mathfrak f\in G(\Q)$.

raw_source_formulation: Fp fibre functor is neutral; geometric isocrystal gerbe is not
exact_canonical_statement_tex:
SA05:A:crystalline: The warning about $\Z$ and $\widehat\Z$ [Proved; Lead A2 is false in its proposed nonneutral interpretation over $\F_p$]. Over $\F_p$, an isocrystal is a finite-dimensional $\Q_p$-vector space with an invertible \emph{linear} operator. Forgetting the operator is an exact faithful tensor functor to $\Q_p$-vector spaces. Thus $T_p$, after this forgetting, really is a fibre functor over $\Q_p$. Its Frobenius action generally does not extend continuously from $\Z$ to $\widehat\Z$. Over $\overline{\F}_p$ the realization instead takes values in the $\Q_p$-linear category $\mathcal R_p$ of isocrystals on $B=W(\overline{\F}_p)[1/p]$. Its fibre-functor gerbe has band $D(\Q)$ and class $\beta_p$ characterized by \[ \operatorname{inv}_p\bigl(s_*(\beta_p)\bigr)=s\pmod\Z, \qquad s\in\Q=X^*(D(\Q)). \] It is not neutral over $\Q_p$.

SA05:A:eta: The Artin torsor and the connecting map [Proved under the stated Tate hypothesis; the Artin calculation is unconditional]. For the Artin--Tate rigidification of Proposition~\ref{A:rigidification}, let $\eta_p=\operatorname{Isom}^{\otimes}(T_p|_{\mathrm{Artin}},F^0_p)$, with the right action on the source; extend it by the trivial Tate factor. Under \[ H^1(\Q_p,G/H)=H^1(\Q_p,\widehat\Z) =\Hom_{\rm cts}(G_{\Q_p},\widehat\Z), \] it is the unramified quotient. Arithmetic local Frobenius maps to $+1$ when the canonical motivic Frobenius is the generator $+1$. The opposite isomorphism torsor has value $-1$ and gives $\xi_p=-\partial(\eta_p^{\mathrm{op}})$ instead. The class of the rigidified gerbe is \[ \xi_p=\partial(\eta_p),\qquad \partial:H^1(\Q_p,G/H)\longrightarrow H^2(\Q_p,H). \]

exact_canonical_statement_tex:
SA05:A:compacthasse: Compact real tori satisfy the degree-two Hasse principle [Proved unconditionally]. If $T/\Q$ is a torus compact over $\R$, with character lattice $L$, then $\Sha^2(\Q,T)=0$. In fact \[ H^2(\Q,T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_v H^2(\Q_v,T). \]

SA05:A:hasse: The global class really is locally determined [Proved unconditionally for the band in Theorem~\ref{A:band]. } For $H^0=D(M)$ one has \[ \Sha^2(\Q,H^0)=0,\qquad H^2(\R,H^0)=0. \] For a finite place $v$, there is a canonical identification \[ H^2(\Q_v,H^0)=\Hom\bigl(M^{G_{\Q_v}},\Q/\Z\bigr). \] More precisely, for any cofinal countable increasing sequence of Galois-stable lattices $L_n\subset M$, and $T_n=D(L_n)$, \[ H^2(\Q,H^0)=\varprojlim_n H^2(\Q,T_n) =\varprojlim_n\bigoplus_v H^2(\Q_v,T_n). \] These equalities are conclusions of the proof, not definitions of cohomology. The assertion in A.3 that $\Sha^2$ of an arbitrary protorus is simply a limit of finite-level $\Sha^2$ is not a valid general rule.

Suppose that the prime-to-$p$ realizations form one object over the finite adeles away from $p$, and that this adelic object's Artin restriction is isomorphic to $F^0\otimes\mathbb A_f^p$, not just separately at each place. At $p$ fix the Artin restriction of the ordinary crystalline $\Q_p$ fibre functor, namely the unramified Artin torsor computed in Proposition~\ref{A:eta}. raw_source_formulation: Component groups distinguish the bands
exact_canonical_statement_tex:
SA05:A:comparison: The correct comparison, and the strict-band counterexample [Strict equivalence with band $H$ or $G$ refuted; corrected equivalence proved under the stated hypotheses]. Let $\mathscr H$ be the Artin--Tate rigidified gerbe of class $\xi_0$. Its pushout along $H\hookrightarrow P=G^0$ is the pseudomotivic $P$-gerbe of \citet[Theorem 3.29 and Theorem 3.31]{AMilne1994}, with the inverse-limit and adelic corrections of \citet[Theorem 6.3 and Definition 6.6]{AMilne2003}. Equivalently it is the gerbe obtained by rigidifying only the Artin fibre functor $F^0$, and under the motivic hypotheses it is the gerbe of motives over $\overline{\F}_p$. There is no band-preserving equivalence of the $H$-gerbe itself or of the full $G$-gerbe with that $P$-gerbe. Their bands have component groups $\mu_2$, $\widehat\Z$, and $1$, respectively. The morphisms that do exist are pushouts \[ \mathscr H\longrightarrow\mathscr P \longrightarrow\mathscr G, \qquad H\hookrightarrow P\hookrightarrow G. \]

SA05:A:dictionary: Dictionary between gerbes and groupoids [Proved]. Let $\mathscr P$ be a $P$-gerbe over $\Q$ and choose $x\in\mathscr P(\overline\Q)$. Its groupoid over $\Spec(\overline\Q)\times_{\Spec\Q}\Spec(\overline\Q)$ is the sheaf of isomorphisms between the two pullbacks of $x$. Its diagonal kernel is $P_{\overline\Q}$. The class in Theorem~\ref{A:class} defines an $H$-gerbe over $\Q$ with exactly the prescribed local classes. It is unique up to $H$-equivalence. The group of isomorphism classes of its band-preserving self-equivalences is \[ H^1(\Q,H)=\Q^\times/\Q^{\times2}\times \frac{\prod_n T_n(\Q)} {\{(a_n f_n(a_{n+1})^{-1})_n:(a_n)_n\in\prod_nT_n(\Q)\}}, \] for the explicit lattice exhaustion in Theorem~\ref{A:hasse}; $f_n:T_{n+1}\to T_n$ is its transition. SA05:A:lefschetz: What the Lefschetz category actually supplies [Proved unconditionally; equality of its band with $P$ is refuted]. Let $\operatorname{LMot}(\overline{\F}_p)$ be the category generated by abelian varieties, with correspondences generated by divisor classes and with the ordinary Tannakian commutativity constraint. It is a semisimple Tannakian category. Its band is \[ L=\mathop{\prod}_{\Pi}^{\Gm} L_\Pi,\qquad X^*(L_\Pi)=\Z^{\Pi}/ \{f:c f=f,\ \textstyle\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}f(\pi)=0\}, \] where $\Pi$ runs through the geometric simple isogeny classes, identified with Galois orbits of integral weight-one Weil germs. The fibre product identifies every multiplier $[\pi]+[c\pi]$. In particular $L$ is commutative, but it is not the Weil-number protorus $P$ in general. Compatible powers of Frobenius generate a subgroup $P\hookrightarrow L$. Prime-to-$p$ realization and crystalline realization, the weight and Tate morphisms, and the real obstruction are available unconditionally. The claimed identification of the entire character group with Weil numbers, full Frobenius-centralizer faithfulness for arbitrary tensor objects, and the resulting formula for $H^0$ cannot simply be transferred to this smaller-correspondence category.

SA05:A:kisin: The unconditional gerbes used in Kisin's paper [Known construction; the signed dictionary proved and independently checked]. Kisin's quasi-motivic gerbe has a band $Q$ defined by a universal condition on real and $p$-adic cocharacters. Its pushout by $Q\twoheadrightarrow P$ is the pseudomotivic gerbe, with the same $P$ and the same local realization morphisms as above. This construction is unconditional. It supplies a Tannakian category of representations of that gerbe; identifying that category with all numerical motives is a separate claim with the hypotheses of A.1. The quasi-motivic band $Q$ itself is not a replacement name for $G$, $H$, or $P$.

SA05:prop:B-phantom-gate: The remaining universal assertion is exactly a phantom-motive gate [Proved equivalence; the equivalent universal assertion remains unresolved]. Assume Tate surjectivity and semisimplicity at eigenvalue one for every smooth projective variety over \(\F_q\), in every codimension. Then the following universal statements are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item The integral Weil--etale comparison holds for all varieties, degrees and twists, and all these integral groups are finitely generated. \item Rational equivalence equals numerical equivalence on all rational Chow groups. \item There is no nonzero rational Chow motive \(P\) whose image \(\bar P\) in numerical motives is zero. \item Every rational Chow motive belongs to the category generated by abelian and Artin motives. \end{enumerate} In particular, the missing assertion in B.1 can be expressed without an unspecified regulator or unspecified comparison map: it is the vanishing of numerical Chow phantoms. The Tate and semisimplicity hypotheses alone have not been shown to imply that vanishing here.

SA05:prop:B-diagonal-Chow-gate: A smaller index set for the remaining Chow comparison [Proved reduction; the restricted cycle-injectivity assertion remains unresolved]. Keep the universal Tate and eigenvalue-one semisimplicity hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:B-phantom-gate}. Fix \(\ell\ne p\). The universal comparison in that proposition is equivalent to injectivity of the cycle map only for the pairs \[ \dim X=2m-1,\qquad \operatorname{CH}^{m}(X)_\Q\otimes\Q_\ell \longrightarrow H^{2m}(\bar X,\Q_\ell(m)), \qquad m\ge2. \tag{B.9a} \] Here all smooth projective varieties in the displayed dimensions, over all finite extensions under consideration, are quantified. There is also a dimension-preserving version: to obtain Beilinson's injectivity in every codimension for varieties of dimension at most \(D\), it suffices to prove it for \[ 3\le d\le D,\qquad 2\le i\le\lceil d/2\rceil. \tag{B.9b} \] The first still undecided ordinary-Chow assertion in either range is codimension two on threefolds. Under the fixed Tate hypotheses, that assertion is equivalent to \[ H^4(F_0\mathbb P^4_{\overline{\F}_q},\Q_\ell(3))^ {\Gal(\overline{\F}_q/\F_q)}=0, \tag{B.9c} \] where \(H^a(F_0Y,\Q_\ell(b))\) means the colimit of continuous \(\ell\)-adic cohomology over dense open subsets of \(Y\). It is not defined by tensoring the Milnor \(K\)-group of the function field with \(\Q_\ell\).

The defect \(\delta_{K,\ell}(0)\) is exactly the Leopoldt defect. For \(n<0\), writing \(m=1-n\), it is exactly the dimension of the kernel of the \(\ell\)-adic regulator \[ K_{2m-1}(\mathcal O_K)^{(m)}\otimes\Q_\ell \longrightarrow\bigoplus_{v\mid\ell}K_v .\tag{B.12} \] In particular, replacing every defect in (B.10) by zero is equivalent, at the indicated \((K,\ell,n)\), to Leopoldt for \(n=0\), or to Schneider's regulator-injectivity conjecture at \(m=1-n\) for \(n<0\).

SA05:thm:B-all-bases-surface-gate: The universal all-base finiteness gate [Proved equivalence; the surface Tate assertion is unresolved]. Fix distinct primes \(p\) and \(\ell\). SA05:c:r7-audit: The R7 hypotheses used in this Part [Used and rechecked, with its internal-Hom counterexample confirmed]. We checked the proof in the supplied reading, \S\S2.1--2.3, against 12:150--158. The conditional construction there is not a construction of a faithful realization on all Chow motives: it first quotients by the chosen homological equivalence, assumes its equality with numerical equivalence and the stated positivity, and then takes the semisimple envelope. Our Chow assertions above do not use this conditional passage. In particular it cannot be used to kill the homologically zero K3 determinant. The sign correction is forced by the cross-product formula: interchanging a class of degree $a$ with one of degree $b$ multiplies it by $(-1)^{ab}$. Thus the original realization is symmetric into graded vector spaces with that commutativity constraint. This is the convention used in our Frobenius equivalence. A level filtration by thick subcategories yields a direct-sum level decomposition only when the ambient category is semisimple; then we group the simple constituents according to their least allowed twist. Thickness alone gives no splitting of extensions. The geometric level definition of C.4 therefore does not assert a canonical splitting or identify itself with coniveau. The internal-Hom error of 12:156 already occurs in the semisimple effective Tate category with objects finite sums of $\Q(-a)$, $a\geq0$. For every effective $Z$, \[ \Hom(Z\otimes\Q(-1),\Q)=0. \] Hence the effective internal Hom from $\Q(-1)$ to $\Q$ is the zero object. SA05:c:lie-centre: The invariant-centre identity [Proved]. For a pro-reductive group $G$ over a characteristic-zero field, \[ \Hom_G(\mathbf1,\Lie G)=(\Lie G)^G=\Lie Z(G). \] If $G$ is connected, the map from its centre to its abelianization induces an isomorphism on Lie algebras. If $G^\circ$ has protorus abelianization $S$ and $\Gamma=G/G^\circ$, then \[ (\Lie G)^G=(\Lie S)^\Gamma. \] The invariant condition under $\Gamma$ cannot be discarded.

SA05:c:serre-centre: Lead C3 with its arithmetic action [Proved under the stated Serre-quotient hypothesis]. Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\Q$, embedded in $\C$, and let $K_0$ be the algebraic closure of $\Q$ in $K$. Suppose that the geometric connected motivic group is pro-reductive, that its maximal protorus quotient is the full Serre protorus $S$, and that the action of $\Gal(\overline K/K)$ on this quotient is the usual action through $\Gal(\overline\Q/K_0)$. If $E$ is the largest CM subfield of $K_0$, then \[ \dim_\Q (\Lie G)^G= \begin{cases}1+[E:\Q]/2,&E\text{ exists},\\1,&K_0\text{ has no CM subfield}. \end{cases} \] These hypotheses hold for the full category of motivated motives of abelian type, including Artin motives. The conclusion concerns the full arithmetic adjoint invariants; the centre of the geometric connected group alone is generally an infinite-dimensional pro-vector space.

SA05:c:finite-field-lie: The finite-field analytic/algebraic distinction [Proved counterexample to the one-dimensional algebraic reading]. Let $E/\F_5$ have equation $y^2=x^3-x$. It is smooth since its discriminant $64$ is nonzero modulo $5$. It has eight rational points, so geometric Frobenius has polynomial $T^2+2T+5$ on $H^1$ and eigenvalues $\pi=-1+2i$, $\bar\pi=-1-2i$. Its algebraic Frobenius torus is \[ T=\operatorname{Res}_{\Q(i)/\Q}\Gm, \qquad\dim T=2. \] Indeed the two primes of $\Q(i)$ above $5$ give valuations $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ on $(\pi,\bar\pi)$; hence $\pi^a\bar\pi^b=1$ implies $a=b=0$. There is consequently no character cutting out a proper algebraic subgroup containing Frobenius. The adjoint action of $T$ is trivial, so its whole Lie algebra is algebraic, but it is two-dimensional. On the other hand, for $\ell=3$ a suitable positive power of $\pi$ belongs to $1+3\Z_3[i]$. The analytic closure of the cyclic Frobenius subgroup has Lie algebra $\Q_3\log(\pi^N)$, of dimension one. The logarithm is nonzero because $\pi$ is not a root of unity. This is the distinction made by Serre in his letter of 8 September 1964, printed p.~202 of \citet{c_grothendieckserre}. Thus ``tout'' on 12:59 is valid for the adjoint Lie algebra of a commutative algebraic motivic band, as in the finite-field category under the Tate hypotheses of Part A; the accompanying identification with a single $\Q(0)$ does not describe that algebraic Lie object. Treating an analytic one-dimensional image as the motivic Lie algebra is an error, not an unconditional proof of a finite-field motivic assertion.

SA05:c:threefold-pairing-kernel: The exact surface-pairing obstruction in dimension three [Proved reduction; the remaining primitive pairing is unresolved]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a projective strictly semistable model of a smooth projective threefold $X$ over a mixed-characteristic local field with finite residue field $k$, and let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Write $Y^{(r)}$ for the disjoint union, over $\bar k$, of the $r$-fold intersections of distinct components of its special fibre. All cohomology below has coefficients $\Q_\ell$. Put \[ A=H^2(Y^{(1)}),\quad U=H^2(Y^{(2)}),\quad B=H^0(Y^{(3)})(-1),\quad Z=H^0(Y^{(4)})(-1). \] Use the signed restriction and Gysin maps of the weight spectral sequence, and define \[ \begin{split} R&=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\rho_A:A\longrightarrow U\bigr),\\ K_0&=R\cap\gamma_B \ker\bigl(\rho_B:B\longrightarrow Z\bigr),\\ b(u,v)&=\sum_{S\subset Y^{(2)}}\operatorname{Tr}_S(u_Sv_S) \ \in\Q_\ell(-2). \end{split} \] Then $K_0\subset\operatorname{rad}(b|_R)$, and there is a Galois-equivariant isomorphism \begin{equation} \ker\!\left( N:\operatorname{Gr}^W_4H^3(X_{\bar K})(1) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Gr}^W_2H^3(X_{\bar K}) \right) \simeq \frac{\operatorname{rad}(b|_R)}{K_0}. \end{equation} Consequently the first remaining C.4 endpoint assertion is equivalent to nondegeneracy of the induced form on $R/K_0$. Choose a relatively ample class $L$. The same assertion is equivalent to nondegeneracy of the surface intersection form on \begin{equation} R_{\rm prim} =R\cap \ker\bigl( L:H^2(Y^{(2)})\longrightarrow H^4(Y^{(2)})(1) \bigr). \end{equation} In particular the remaining condition involves only a primitive restriction image in the degree-two cohomology of the double-intersection surfaces. It does not require the unknown nondegeneracy of an additional Gysin image.

SA05:c:universal-trait-weight-equivalence: The universal trait endpoint and weight--monodromy [Proved equivalence; the universal assertions remain unresolved]. Fix a residue characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. We consider finite extensions $K/\Q_p$, with finite residue field, and geometric $\ell$-adic cohomology. The following universal assertions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item Weight--monodromy holds for $H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$ for every smooth projective $Z/K$ and every $j\geq0$. \item For every smooth projective $j$-fold $Z/K$, $H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)^{I_K}$ has weights at most $j$. \item The assertion in (2) holds for the generic fibres of projective strictly semistable models over $\mathcal O_K$. \end{enumerate} In (2) the stated space is the closed geometric stalk of $u_*H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$ for the open immersion $u:\Spec K\hookrightarrow\Spec\mathcal O_K$. Thus it is exactly the dimension-normalized, degree-zero trait endpoint. For an individual $j$-fold, after a finite extension making its inertia action unipotent, it suffices to test the bound $rj$ on $\ker N$ in $\bigwedge^r H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$ for $1\leq r\leq j+1$. Each such test is a direct-summand test in the middle cohomology $H^{rj}(Z^r_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$. A failure of weight--monodromy therefore yields a trait-endpoint failure on one of these powers, or on a projective semistable alteration of that power.

SA05:c:vz-positive: The positive purity range [Known, with its application proved]. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a two-dimensional regular local ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ and let $U=\Spec R\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$. Every abelian scheme over $U$ extends uniquely over $R$ if $p\notin\mathfrak m^p$. In particular the sufficient absolute ramification bound is $e\leq p-1$, including equality. More generally the same conclusion holds under the complete faithfully flat quotient condition of Vasiu--Zink Theorem 3. If an abelian variety over $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ has good reduction at every height-one prime, these conclusions apply to it. Equivalently, at each such prime one may use the prime-to-residue-characteristic unramifiedness test of the N\'eron--Ogg--Shafarevich criterion.

SA05:c:explicit-bad-reduction: An explicit abelian-surface counterexample at $p=2$ [Proved refutation of the unrestricted criterion]. Let $k=\overline\F_2$ and \[ R=W(k)[[u,v]]/(2-uv),\qquad K=\operatorname{Frac}(R),\qquad \mathfrak m=(u,v). \] Consider the elliptic schemes \begin{align*} E_1:&\quad Y^2Z+(u+v^2)XYZ+YZ^2=X^3,\\ E_2:&\quad Y^2Z+(v+u^2)XYZ+YZ^2=X^3, \end{align*} with origins $[0:1:0]$, and put $A=E_1\times_R E_2$. The sections \[ P_v=[-v:1:v^3]\in E_1(R),\qquad P_u=[-u:1:u^3]\in E_2(R) \] have order two on the generic fibre. Let $C_K\subset A_K$ be the order-two subgroup generated by $(P_v,P_u)$, and define the abelian surface \[ B_K=A_K/C_K. \] Then $B_K$ has good reduction at every height-one prime of $R$, hence its $T_\ell$ is unramified at every height-one point of $S_\ell=\Spec R[1/\ell]$ for every prime $\ell$, but it does not extend to an abelian scheme over $R$. The schematic closure of $C_K$ in $A$ is explicitly nonflat.

SA05:c:ell-independence-gate: The remaining general-motive claim [Unresolved in the general motivic category]. Theorem~\ref{c:ell-independence-abelian} settles the whole abelian-type assertion, including its finite-inertia descent. The direct argument from an arbitrary original generator would still be invalid: $\bigwedge^2H^1(E)=\Q_\ell(-1)$ is unramified at a place of residue characteristic different from $\ell$, even when $E$ has bad reduction. The weak-lift lemma and the trace argument are what repair that inference. For Andr\'e motivated motives, Theorem~\ref{c:motivated-unramified-rank-reduction} supplies a second named sufficient hypothesis: independence of homological equivalence for rational cycles on all smooth projective varieties over $\overline{\F}_p$. It controls the monodromy ranks and the finite inertia action, but remains conditional on that finite-field conjecture. Corollary~\ref{c:motivated-abelian-strata-unramified} gives the stated unconditional geometric case only when all auxiliary strata have the required algebraic abelian-type presentations. Neither result proves a converse to the finite-field conjecture. For general motives, another precise named sufficient conjecture is Fontaine's motivic Weil--Deligne compatibility conjecture: \citet[\S2.4.3, Conjecture $C_{\mathrm{WD}}(X,m)$, p.~342, and its motivic formulation in \S2.4.7, pp.~344--345]{c_fontaine1994pst}. The motivic formulation is required to retain the specified projector; compatibility of an unlabelled ambient cohomology representation alone does not identify every prescribed summand. Write the local Weil--Deligne data as $(r_\ell,N_\ell)$, with $r_\ell$ of finite inertial image. On an open subgroup of inertia the actual action is $\exp(t_\ell(\tau)N_\ell)$, where the tame character has infinite image. Consequently \[ M_\ell\text{ is unramified at }v \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\ell=0\ \text{ and }\ r_\ell|_{I_v}=1. \] Both conditions are invariant under extension of coefficient fields and isomorphism of Weil--Deligne representations. Thus Fontaine's compatibility, which only requires isomorphism after common coefficient extension and not a chosen rational form, implies the requested independence. His weaker monodromy-graded character formulation in \S2.4.5 also suffices: the characters at the identity determine whether the monodromy filtration is concentrated in degree zero, equivalently $N=0$; after that, the finite inertia character detects triviality. This proves an implication, not the exact equivalence requested in the question. Algebraically, the representations trivial on a subgroup $J\subset G$ detect its closed normal closure, not the whole inertia representation. Even all tensor tests do not formally recover the nilpotent's Jordan type: in $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, both $E_{12}$ and $E_{12}+E_{23}$ act nontrivially in every nontrivial algebraic representation, since the differential's kernel is an ideal in the simple Lie algebra. Their ranks differ. The accompanying notes give compatible abstract Weil--Deligne pairs and a matrix certificate; no such pair is asserted to come from a global motive, and it is not a motivic counterexample. The theorem of \citet[Theorem 5.1]{c_commelin2019} concerns abelian motives and quasi-compatibility; by itself it does not supply finite-inertia traces for an arbitrary motive at a bad place. Similarly the $G$-valued expectation of \citet[Conjecture 1.1]{c_kisinzhou2025} is stronger than the asserted triviality test. A proof in the general motivic category, or an exact equivalence with a published named conjecture of precisely the required strength, remains an outstanding assertion, recorded separately from the now proved abelian-type theorem.

The theorem removes the algebraic-projector limitation of the earlier sufficient-conjecture implication by using Andr\'e's finite algebraic-and-Lefschetz presentation. An arbitrary absolute-Hodge projector is not thereby proved motivated, and a numerical projector is not thereby supplied with a realization-compatible presentation. No converse from unramifiedness independence to the finite-field rank conjecture has been proved. The geometric construction needed to encode an arbitrary finite-field correspondence in the monodromy of a number-field variety remains separate.

exact_canonical_statement_tex:
SA06:B.1a: B.1a. Realization in every weight (Known; derivation supplied).. For every algebraic integer $\lambda$ of weight $i\geq0$, namely $|\sigma(\lambda)|=q^{i/2}$ for every complex embedding $\sigma$, there exists a smooth projective $X/\mathbb F_q$ such that $\lambda$ occurs on $H^i(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},\mathbb Q_\ell)$. For $i>0$ we may take $X=A_\alpha^i$, where $\alpha^i=\lambda$ and $A_\alpha$ belongs to the Honda--Tate isogeny class of $\alpha$. Thus the weak conjecture holds with the explicit exponent $m=1$ in every weight; no class number or unit index enters that exponent.

SA06:B.1b: B.1b. Explicit construction data and the semisimple motive (Proved, using Honda--Tate and numerical semisimplicity).. The preceding prescription specifies $X$ by a uniquely determined isogeny class and a product operation; every member of that class works. There is also a terminating, although inefficient, construction by equations. Compute the minimal polynomial $P_\alpha$ and the division algebra index $d$ from the local invariants in \citet[Th\'eor\`eme~1(ii)]{Tate1971}. The desired class has Frobenius polynomial $P_\alpha^d$ and dimension $g=d[\mathbb Q(\alpha):\mathbb Q]/2$. Enumerate projective equations over $\mathbb F_q$ together with regular group-law and inverse-law presentations, retaining smooth, geometrically connected, commutative group varieties of dimension $g$. These tests reduce to ideal membership, smoothness, and finite-type algebra over a finite field. Every abelian variety has such a finite presentation. Choose $\ell^a$ larger than twice every coefficient bound $\binom{2g}{j}q^{j/2}$ for its Frobenius polynomial. The finite \'etale group scheme $A[\ell^a]$ and its Frobenius action can be computed by finite algebra over finite fields. Its characteristic polynomial modulo $\ell^a$ has a unique integral lift within those bounds. Stop at the first polynomial $P_\alpha^d$. Honda--Tate proves termination. This gives an effective specification for every input $\lambda$; the general enumeration has not been run. The numerical motive $N=h^1(A_\alpha)^{\otimes i}$ is semisimple by \citet[Theorem~1]{Jannsen1992}. It is homogeneous of weight $i$ and has $\lambda$ as an intrinsic Frobenius eigenvalue. One does not need an unproved realization functor on all numerical motives for this last assertion. The K\"unneth projectors of an abelian variety are algebraic; the kernel from homological to numerical endomorphisms is nilpotent by \citet[Corollary~1]{Jannsen1992}. Frobenius acts semisimply on the cohomology of $A_\alpha^i$. Its nonzero spectral idempotent belonging to the minimal polynomial of $\lambda$ therefore cannot disappear in a nilpotent ideal. Consequently that eigenvalue remains on $N$. This proves the semisimple-motive form of the weak conjecture with $m=1$.

Sufficiency is B.1a. Necessity is \citet[Th\'eor\`eme~(1.6), p.~276]{Deligne1974}, applied to each smooth projective $X$. In particular weight $2$ is obtained from $\alpha^2=\lambda$ and $A_\alpha^2$, and weight $3$ from $\alpha^3=\lambda$ and $A_\alpha^3$. Real numbers $\lambda=\pm q^{i/2}$, all supersingular cases, and all Jacobi sums which satisfy the stated Weil-integer condition fall under the same proof. There is no omitted exception for $p=2$, $p=3$, or nonsquare $q$. If geometric connectedness were imposed also in degree zero, the exact degree-zero set would instead be $\{1\}$; that is not the convention of the question.

SA06:B.3b: B.3b. The $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-23})$ test, including an equation (Proved and computed).. Put $L=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-23})$, $\omega=(1+\sqrt{-23})/2$, $\lambda=1+\omega$, and $q=2$. Then \[ \omega^2-\omega+6=0,\qquad \lambda^2-3\lambda+8=0,\qquad \lambda\bar\lambda=8. \] The prime $\mathfrak p=(2,\omega-1)$ satisfies $(\lambda)=\mathfrak p^3$: the conjugate prime $(2,\omega)$ does not divide $\lambda$, and its absolute norm is $8$. No algebraic integer of $L$ has norm $2$, since \[ N(a+b\omega)=a^2+ab+6b^2 =\left(a+\frac b2\right)^2+\frac{23b^2}{4} \] cannot equal $2$ for integers $a,b$. Hence the fixed-field factorization into weight-one Weil $2$-integers is impossible, although unrestricted realization is possible. We can also verify $h_L=3$ without relying on a table of quadratic forms. The Minkowski bound is $(2/\pi)\sqrt{23}<4$, so every ideal class has a representative of norm $1$, $2$, or $3$. Both $2$ and $3$ split, and $(\omega)=(2,\omega)(3,\omega)$ identifies the class of one prime over $3$ with the inverse class of one prime over $2$. The latter class is nontrivial by the norm-$2$ calculation and has cube one by $(\lambda)=\mathfrak p^3$. The possible representative classes are exactly its three powers. Here is an actual variety over $\mathbb F_2$. Let $\mathbb F_8=\mathbb F_2[t]/(t^3+t+1)$ and let \[ E/\mathbb F_8:\quad y^2+xy=x^3+x^2+(t+1). \] Its projective closure is nonsingular: in the affine chart a singular point would have $x=0$ and then $y=0$ from the two derivatives, which contradicts $t+1\ne0$; the unique point at infinity is nonsingular. Thus it is a smooth plane cubic with a rational origin. Exhaustive enumeration gives five affine points and the point at infinity, so $\#E(\mathbb F_8)=6$. The Frobenius polynomial is $T^2-3T+8$. Set $A=\operatorname{Res}_{\mathbb F_8/\mathbb F_2}E$, an abelian threefold. Its $H^1$ is the induced representation, so its Frobenius polynomial is $T^6-3T^3+8$; this is precisely the restriction-of-scalars calculation of \citet[\S3, Lemma~1]{Tate1971}. In fact $X=A$ already suffices. On $H^3(A)=\bigwedge^3H^1(A)$ the characteristic polynomial is \[ (T^2-3T+8)(T^6-24T^3+512)^3. \] To verify this identity without approximating roots, the supplied program forms the $20\times20$ exterior-cube matrix of the integral companion matrix of $T^6-3T^3+8$ and factors its characteristic polynomial over $\mathbb Q$. This proves that $\lambda$ occurs on $H^3(A_{\overline{\mathbb F}_2},\mathbb Q_\ell)$ for every $\ell\ne2$. The same program enumerates the three reduced primitive forms of discriminant $-23$, agreeing with $h_L=3$.

exact_canonical_statement_tex:
SA06:B.4c: B.4c. The purported unpowered canonical point is not defined (Refuted; correction to R7).. There is no inclusion-valued homomorphism $M_0/\mu(L)\to L^\times$, $[u]\mapsto u$. Already $[1]=[-1]$ while $1\ne-1$. Consequently the ``point of $D(M_0/\mathrm{torsion})$ whose evaluation on $M_0$ is the inclusion'' used in R7 and its cited proof does not exist. This is a type error, independently of any class-group issue. More invariantly, the genuine tautological point is $f_0\in D(M_0)(\mathbb Q)$, the Galois-equivariant map $u\mapsto u$. It does not lie in $D(M_0)^0$, because its restriction to $\mu(L)$ is not trivial. Thus it has no lift from a connected norm-one torus into that identity component, for any $q$. For a concrete counterexample with vanishing divisor cokernel take $L=\mathbb Q(i)$ and $p=5$. With $a=(2+i)/(2-i)$ we have $M_0=\mu_4\times\langle a\rangle$, $C_{L,5}=0$; nevertheless $f_0(i)=i\ne1$, while every point of $D(M_0)^0$ evaluates $i$ as $1$. The assertion cannot be repaired merely by assuming that the divisor isogeny is an isomorphism. There is a second distinction. If $M=M(q,L)$ and $G=D(M)$, with $\varepsilon$ corresponding to $q\in M$, then \[ X^*((G/j(\mathbb G_m))^0)=M_0/\mu(L),\qquad X^*((\ker\varepsilon)^0)=(M/\mathbb Z q)/\mathrm{torsion}. \] These lattices are naturally isogenous, but cannot be identified without accounting for the possible factor $2$. On $M_0$ the natural anti-divisor map $m\mapsto\operatorname{div}(m/\bar m)$ is $2\operatorname{div}$, not $\operatorname{div}$.

SA06:B.4d: B.4d. Canonical powered points and an exact lifting criterion (Proved).. Put $r=|\mu(L)|$ and $T=D(M_0/\mu(L))$. For every integer $k$ divisible by $r$ there is a canonical point $g_k\in T(\mathbb Q)$ defined by $[u](g_k)=u^k$. Divisibility by $r$ is necessary and sufficient for this formula to be independent of the representative. Suppose $\tau\mathfrak p\ne\mathfrak p$, let $D_{\mathfrak p}\subset\operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbb Q)$ be its decomposition group, and put $L_0=L^{D_{\mathfrak p}}$, $K_0=L_0\cap K$. Set \[ S_0=\operatorname{Res}_{K_0/\mathbb Q} \operatorname{Res}^{1}_{L_0/K_0}\mathbb G_m. \] The inclusion $\Lambda\subset D^-$ defines a $\mathbb Q$-isogeny $\phi:S_0\to T$. For $z\in L_0^\times$ with $z\bar z=1$ and $D=\sum n_{\mathfrak s}\mathfrak s\in D^-$, define \[ e_z(D)=\prod_{\mathfrak s\in S/\langle\tau\rangle} \sigma_{\mathfrak s}(z)^{n_{\mathfrak s}}, \qquad\sigma_{\mathfrak s}\mathfrak p=\mathfrak s. \] The product is independent of orientations and of representatives of the cosets $\sigma_{\mathfrak s}D_{\mathfrak p}$. Then the full set of rational lifts of $g_k$ is \[ \boxed{\ \{z\in L_0^\times: z\bar z=1,\quad e_z(\operatorname{div}u_j)=u_j^k\ (1\leq j\leq s)\}\ }, \] where $u_1,\ldots,u_s$ is any basis of $M_0/\mu(L)$ with chosen representatives. When nonempty it is a right torsor under $\ker\phi(\mathbb Q)$, acting by multiplication.

SA06:B.4e: B.4e. A finite arithmetic test and explicit exponent (Proved).. In B.4d every lift satisfies \[ \operatorname{div}_L(z)=k(\mathfrak p-\tau\mathfrak p). \] For a fixed $k$, first test whether an element of $L_0$ with that divisor and norm one exists. Integral ideals, class relations, and the unit norm quotient in B.4a give exactly this test; the valuations must also be divisible by the ramification index of $L/L_0$. If none exists, there is no lift. If $z_0$ exists, every candidate is $z_0\eta$ with $\eta\in\mu(L_0)$. Test the finitely many candidates in the equations of B.4d. This determines the answer, with no remaining existence problem or omitted sign. For a universal sufficient exponent, let $h$ be the exponent of $\operatorname{Cl}(L)$ and $d=|D_{\mathfrak p}|$. Then \[ \boxed{\ k=2hdr\ } \] always works. In particular the full criterion is much stronger than an ``if and only if the isogeny is an isomorphism'' claim.

SA06:B.4f: B.4f. Normalization inside $\ker\varepsilon$ and field extension (Proved; the literal unpowered request is refuted).. The natural map to $U^0=(\ker\varepsilon)^0$ is instead dual to \[ (M/\mathbb Zq)/\mathrm{torsion}\longrightarrow D^-, \qquad[m]\longmapsto\operatorname{div}(m/\bar m). \] It is injective with finite cokernel: its kernel before taking the torsion-free quotient consists exactly of $m$ whose $m/\bar m$ is a root of unity, and its image contains $2\Lambda$. For an integer $k$ divisible by $r$, the rational normalized point \[ f^{2k}j(q^{-k})\in U^0(\mathbb Q) \] evaluates a character $m$ as $(m/\bar m)^k$. Its lifting criterion is B.4d with $u_j$ replaced by generators of $\{m/\bar m:m\in M\}$. The same construction of B.4e lifts it for $k=2hdr$. This gives a fully typed replacement for the erroneous unpowered normalization on 15:112 and in R7. We stress the direction of base change. In the category obtained by extending a fixed object from $\mathbb F_q$ to $\mathbb F_{q^k}$, Frobenius is replaced by its $k$th power, and the character map is $u\mapsto u^k$. The powered assertions above apply in exactly that sense. Merely replacing the symbol $q$ by $q^k$ while retaining the full norm-one group $M_0(q,L)=M_0(p,L)$ changes neither the lattice nor its cokernel and does not create an unpowered canonical point. For instance $C_{\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-23}),2}=\mathbb Z/3$ for every $q=2^n$. This distinction is also why the normalized groups $W_0^L(q)$ in \citet[Proposition~2.27]{Milne1994}, which impose an additional integrality condition on normalized absolute values, must not be substituted for the $M_0(q)$ of 15:110.

exact_canonical_statement_tex: SA06:C.1n: C.1n (Proved: the endpoint image criterion is exactly the universal standard conjecture $D$).. We first work over $\mathbb C$ with rational coefficients. Fix integers $n\ge0$ and $0\le r\le n$. Let $\mathcal I_{n,r}$ mean the following assertion: for every smooth projective connected $n$-fold $X$, every smooth projective connected $d$-fold $Y$, every $0\le j\le d$, and every correspondence \[ \Gamma\in\mathrm{CH}^{d+r-j}(Y\times X)_{\mathbb Q}, \] an element $z\in A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ belongs to the image of $\Gamma_*:A^j_{\mathrm{alg}}(Y)\to A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ if and only if its cycle class belongs to the image of \[ \Gamma_*:H^{2j}(Y,\mathbb Q(j)) \longrightarrow H^{2r}(X,\mathbb Q(r)). \] These are the source and degree-shift quantifiers of the image criterion on manuscript page $14{:}46$: its source degree is arbitrary, and the correspondence need not have degree zero. Write $D_{\mathbb C}$ for equality of numerical and Betti homological equivalence on rational cycles of every smooth projective complex variety. Then \begin{equation} \mathcal I_{n,r}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad D_{\mathbb C} \qquad\text{if }r\in\{0,1,n\}. \end{equation} For every $2\le r\le n-1$, the assertion $\mathcal I_{n,r}$ is false by C.1k. If we restrict the target to $X=\mathbb P^n$, its image criterion is equivalent to $D_{\mathbb C}$ for \emph{every} $0\le r\le n$. More precisely, for a \emph{fixed} $X$ and $r$, let $\mathcal I(X,r)$ require the displayed criterion for every source $Y$, source degree $j$, and correspondence $\Gamma$. Then \begin{equation} \mathcal I(X,r)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl(D_{\mathbb C}\ \text{and}\ G^r(X)=0\bigr). \end{equation} \emph{Necessity, including the restricted projective-space target.} Suppose that $D_{\mathbb C}$ fails. Then some smooth projective $d$-fold $Y$ has a numerically trivial rational cycle $a\in\mathrm{CH}^s(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ with $\mathrm{cl}(a)\ne0$. Put $j=d-s$, let $h$ be the hyperplane class on $\mathbb P^n$, and set \[ \Gamma=a\times h^r\in \mathrm{CH}^{s+r}(Y\times\mathbb P^n)_{\mathbb Q}. \] The codimension is $s+r=d+r-j$, as required. The action on cycles is \[ \Gamma_*b=\deg(a\cdot b)h^r=0 \qquad\bigl(b\in A^j_{\mathrm{alg}}(Y)\bigr), \] by numerical triviality. In contrast, Poincar\'e duality supplies $v\in H^{2d-2s}(Y,\mathbb Q(d-s))$ with $\int_Y\mathrm{cl}(a)v=1$. Hence $\Gamma_*v=\mathrm{cl}(h^r)$, although the nonzero cycle class $h^r\in A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(\mathbb P^n)$ is not in the cycle image. This contradicts the proposed criterion. Notice that we neither need nor assert that this cohomological preimage $v$ is algebraic: the criterion itself would force an algebraic preimage, which numerical triviality excludes. The same construction works for any fixed target $X$: take $h$ ample on $X$; its power $h^r$ has nonzero cohomology class, since $\int_Xh^n>0$. Thus $\mathcal I(X,r)$ also implies $D_{\mathbb C}$. Taking $\Gamma=0$ shows separately that $\mathcal I(X,r)$ implies $G^r(X)=0$. \emph{Sufficiency.} Assume $D_{\mathbb C}$. By \citet[Theorem~1, pp.~448--449] {Jannsen1992}, the category of rational numerical motives is semisimple abelian. Betti realization on this category is well defined and faithful: $D_{\mathbb C}$ applies on every product, and K\"unneth together with Poincar\'e duality identifies a correspondence's total cohomology class with its action on all cohomological degrees. Here K\"unneth is only the cohomological decomposition; we do not assume algebraic K\"unneth projectors. We use the convention \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,h(X)(r)) &=A^r_{\mathrm{num}}(X),\\ \operatorname{Hom}(h(Y)(j),h(X)(r)) &=A^{d+r-j}_{\mathrm{num}}(Y\times X). \end{split} \] Thus $\Gamma$ induces a morphism $f:M=h(Y)(j)\to N=h(X)(r)$, and the numerical class of $z$ is a morphism $\beta:\mathbf1\to N$. Semisimplicity gives $g:N\to M$ for which $p=fg$ is a projector onto $\operatorname{im}(f)$ and $pf=f$. If $\mathrm{cl}(z)$ is in the stated cohomological image, then $H((1-p)\beta)=0$. Indeed realization in degree zero of $h(Y)(j)$ and $h(X)(r)$ is precisely the pair of groups in the displayed image criterion. Faithfulness gives $(1-p)\beta=0$, so \[ \beta=f(g\beta). \] Choose a rational cycle $b\in\mathrm{CH}^j(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ representing $g\beta$. We have proved that $\Gamma_*b$ and $z$ are numerically equivalent. In target codimensions $r=0,n$, numerical and algebraic equivalence with rational coefficients are both determined by degree. In codimension $r=1$, the same equality follows from the N\'eron--Severi theorem and the divisor intersection pairing, as recalled in C.1k. Therefore $\Gamma_*b=z$ in $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ in every asserted endpoint case. The converse implication is always given by functoriality of the cycle class. For $X=\mathbb P^n$, the map $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)\to A^r_{\mathrm{num}}(X)$ is an isomorphism in every codimension, so the same proof gives the final restricted-target assertion. For the fixed-target assertion, $D_{\mathbb C}$ identifies numerical and homological equivalence, and $G^r(X)=0$ identifies homological and algebraic equivalence in the specified target group. The same numerical preimage therefore proves \eqref{eq:fixed-target-image-D}. These two equivalences are not restricted to complex geometry. Let $k$ be any algebraically closed field and let $H$ be a fixed Weil cohomology with characteristic-zero coefficient field $F$. Keep rational cycle coefficients, use $F$ in the cohomological image, and define $D_{k,H}$ by equality of numerical and $H$-homological equivalence for rational cycles on every smooth projective $k$-variety. The identical argument proves \[ \mathcal I_{n,r}^{k,H}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ D_{k,H} \qquad(r\in\{0,1,n\}), \] \[ \mathcal I^{k,H}(X,r)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \bigl(D_{k,H}\ \text{and}\ G_H^r(X)=0\bigr), \] where $G_H^r(X)$ is the kernel of the rational-cycle class map into $H^{2r}(X)(r)$. The source functional is evaluated using Poincar\'e duality over $F$; the numerical-motive category and its image splitting still have rational coefficients. Numerical and algebraic equivalence agree rationally for divisors over any algebraically closed field, and degree handles codimensions zero and top. The intermediate-codimension universal counterexamples cited above remain assertions over $\mathbb C$; this extension does not transfer their nonvanishing to positive characteristic. Equations~\eqref{eq:endpoint-image-D}--\eqref{eq:fixed-target-image-D} isolate an exact remaining standard-conjecture gate. It does not prove $D_{\mathbb C}$ and does not replace homological equivalence by algebraic equivalence in intermediate target codimension. It also explains why the absence of a target Griffiths group by itself was insufficient for the image argument in C.1k: the unrestricted source can still detect a failure of $D$.

SA06:C.1j: C.1j (Proved: the exact middle-positivity obstruction over $\mathbb C$).. Let $X/\mathbb C$ be smooth projective of dimension $2m$, and put \[ P^m_{\mathrm{alg},L}(X) =\ker\bigl(L:A^m_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)\longrightarrow A^{m+1}_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)\bigr). \] The form $q(x,y)=(-1)^m\deg(xy)$ is positive semidefinite on this space. Its radical is exactly \begin{equation} \operatorname{rad}(q)= \ker\bigl(L:G^m(X)\longrightarrow G^{m+1}(X)\bigr). \end{equation} Consequently the letter's $B(X,L)$ is equivalent to the injectivity of this particular map on the rational Griffiths group.

SA06:C.1o: C.1o (Proved: projective-space stabilization identifies the exact positivity kernel).. Let $X/\mathbb C$ be smooth projective of dimension $n$, let $h$ be an ample rational divisor class, and put $t=c_1(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^d}(1))$. Suppose that $n+d=2m$ is even. For $0\le d\le n$ set $i=(n-d)/2$. There is an explicit isomorphism \begin{equation} \begin{split} \ker\bigl(h^{d+1}:G^i(X)\longrightarrow G^{i+d+1}(X)\bigr) &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \operatorname{rad}\bigl(q_{X\times\mathbb P^d,h+t}\bigr),\\ z&\longmapsto \sum_{j=0}^{d}(-1)^j h^jz\,t^{d-j}. \end{split} \end{equation} Here $q$ is the middle primitive form of C.1j, with cycles modulo algebraic equivalence and rational coefficients. If $d>n$, that radical is zero. The statement uses the actual product polarization $h+t$; it is unchanged after a positive rational rescaling of either factor.

SA06:C.1p: C.1p (Proved: the exact Beauville-graded positivity test on abelian stabilizations).. Fix a complex abelian variety $A$ of dimension $g$. The following assertions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item the letter's $B$ holds for every even-dimensional $A\times\mathbb P^d$ and every ample class on it; \item $G^r(A)_{(s)}=0$ for every $r$ and every $s\le0$. \end{enumerate} Equivalently, the quotient $B^*(A)=\mathrm{CH}^*(A)_{\mathbb Q}/ \mathrm{CH}^*(A)_{\mathrm{alg},\mathbb Q}$ has no negative Beauville pieces, and its grade-zero cycle map is injective. This is a statement modulo algebraic equivalence. We do not identify it with the corresponding conjectures for the ordinary Chow group.

SA06:C.1q: C.1q (Proved: the exact exceptional polynomial and the ample-pencil test).. Let $M/\mathbb C$ be smooth projective of dimension $2m$, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow M$ be a smooth connected center of codimension $c\ge2$, and put $\pi:X=\operatorname{Bl}_Z(M)\to M$. Write $j:E\hookrightarrow X$ and $p:E\to Z$ for the exceptional divisor and its projection, and set \[ N=N_{Z/M},\qquad \xi=c_1(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(N)}(1)). \] Assume $G^m(M)=G^{m+1}(M)=0$; in particular this holds when $M$ has a Tate Chow motive. Let $L=\pi^*D-bE$ be an ample rational class, so $b>0$, and put $u=i^*D/b$. Define \[ q_N(T)=\sum_{k=0}^{c-1}c_k(N)T^{c-1-k},\qquad c_0(N)=1. \] Then extraction of the last exceptional coefficient gives an isomorphism \begin{equation} \operatorname{rad}(q_{X,L})\simeq \ker\left(q_N(-u):G^{m-c+1}(Z)\longrightarrow G^m(Z)\right). \end{equation} Thus Griffiths classes strictly above the middle degree of a center, by themselves, do not create a primitive middle radical: the controlling degree is \[ m-c+1=\frac{\dim Z-c+2}{2}\le\frac{\dim Z}{2}. \] No condition on the Chern classes of the normal bundle can change that degree constraint.

SA06:C.2h: C.2h (Proved): middle positivity and the positive trace form.. We give the reduction, then specify exactly the additional Lefschetz hypothesis needed for its consequences on correspondences. Let $x\in A_H^r(X)$ be primitive, with $\dim X=n\ge2r$, and let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a smooth complete intersection of dimension $2r$ formed from the chosen hyperplanes. Restriction in degree $2r$ is injective by weak Lefschetz. Moreover $i^*x$ is primitive: the Gysin map out of $H^{2r+2}(Y)$ is injective, by duality with weak Lefschetz in degree $2r-2$, and \[ i_*(L_Y i^*x)=L^{n-2r+1}x=0. \] Thus middle positivity on $Y$ gives, for $x\ne0$, \[ (-1)^r\deg_X(L^{n-2r}x^2) =(-1)^r\deg_Y((i^*x)^2)>0. \] This proves the reduction in \citet[Proposition 3.7]{cyKleiman1968}; its converse is its middle case. No algebraicity of a Lefschetz inverse was used in this paragraph. Now assume the Lefschetz standard conjecture $B_{\rm std}$ for the varieties involved and Hodge standard positivity on their products. The Lefschetz primitive projectors, inverse operators, and star operators are algebraic. If $u$ is an algebraic cohomological correspondence, its adjoint \[ u^\dagger=*_{X}\,{}^t u\,*_{Y} \] (with the standard degree-wise Lefschetz signs) is therefore algebraic. The ordinary trace $\operatorname{Tr}(u^\dagger u)$ is rational and strictly positive for $u\ne0$. Here is the checked computation behind this input, as in \citet[Theorem 3.11]{cyKleiman1968}. Decompose $u$ by the algebraic orthogonal projectors onto Lefschetz strings. The trace norm is the sum of the trace norms of these blocks. Transporting each block to its primitive factors reduces to a primitive class in $P^a(X)\otimes P^b(Y)$, where $a+b$ is even. The product Lefschetz operator is $L_X\otimes1+1\otimes L_Y$; expanding its power contributes the positive binomial factor \[ \binom{n-a+m-b}{n-a}, \qquad n=\dim X,\quad m=\dim Y. \] The trace formula contributes $(-1)^a$, and exchanging the two primitive factors contributes $(-1)^{ab}$. Their product is $+1$ because $a+b$ is even. Up to that positive binomial factor, the block norm is therefore its primitive Hodge intersection norm on $X\times Y$, which is positive by the stated hypothesis. Rationality follows from the correspondence trace formula, an intersection number of rational cycles. This verifies the hypotheses of the finite algebra arguments below; positivity on just $X$, without the relevant products, is not substituted for them. The resulting $\mathbb Q$-algebra $E$ of algebraic endomorphisms is finite dimensional, even before one invokes semisimplicity. To see this directly, choose a maximal linearly independent list $u_1,\ldots,u_s$ over the cohomology coefficient field in the image algebra. The map \[ E\longrightarrow\mathbb Q^s, \qquad u\longmapsto (\operatorname{Tr}(u^\dagger u_1),\ldots, \operatorname{Tr}(u^\dagger u_s)) \] is injective. If all coordinates vanish, express $u$ in the coefficient- field span of the $u_j$ to obtain $\operatorname{Tr}(u^\dagger u)=0$, whence $u=0$. The $u_j$ are also rationally independent, so the injection proves $\dim_{\mathbb Q}E=s$. They are consequently a rational basis as well as a basis after extension to the cohomology coefficient field. In particular that scalar extension of the correspondence algebra remains faithful. This proves finite dimensionality and a positive definite rational trace form. Its extension to $E\otimes\mathbb R$ is positive definite: a negative real direction would give a negative rational direction, and a degenerate rational matrix would have a nonzero rational kernel.

With the hypotheses on all products, the same argument, or the numerical identification and \citet[Theorem 1]{Jannsen1992}, gives the semisimplicity of the idempotent-complete pure homological motive category. Otherwise, at some nonarchimedean place one of them has absolute value greater than one. The power series \[ \sum_{m\ge1}\left(\sum_j\lambda_j^m\right)t^m =-\frac{tP'(t)}{P(t)}, \qquad P(t)=\prod_j(1-\lambda_jt), \] has bounded coefficients at that place and is analytic on $|t|<1$. The rational function on the right has a pole at the reciprocal of such a $\lambda_j$, which lies in that disk. There is no cancellation: a nonzero root of $P$ of multiplicity $e$ contributes a logarithmic pole with nonzero residue proportional to $e$ in characteristic zero. This contradicts the power-series identity. Thus all eigenvalues are integral, and the rational elementary symmetric functions are integers. This is the mechanism in \citet[Proposition 2.6]{cyKleiman1968}; it requires no unproved removal of $p$-denominators. Let $L$ be an ample class defined over $\mathbb F_q$, and extend the scalar algebra from $\mathbb Q$ to $\mathbb Q(\sqrt q)\subset\mathbb R$. The normalized degree-wise operator \[ g=\sum_i q^{-i/2}F_i\pi_i \] is multiplicative, fixes $L$ because $F^*L=qL$, and acts as the identity on top cohomology because the Frobenius morphism has degree $q^n$. Poincar\'e duality therefore gives its transpose as $g^{-1}$. Since $g$ commutes with $L$, with the primitive projectors, and with Lefschetz star, its adjoint in C.2h is also $g^{-1}$: \[ g^\dagger g=1. \] Left multiplication by $g$ on the finite real correspondence algebra is an isometry for the positive trace inner product, since \[ \operatorname{Tr}((ga)^\dagger gb) =\operatorname{Tr}(a^\dagger b). \] It is consequently diagonalizable over $\mathbb C$, with eigenvalues on the unit circle. The left regular representation and the faithful cohomological representation have the same minimal polynomial for an algebra element: a polynomial in that element vanishes in one exactly when it vanishes in the algebra. Hence the same semisimplicity and absolute-value statement holds for $g$ in cohomology. On the invariant left ideal $\pi_iE_{\mathbb R}$, left multiplication by $g$ equals $q^{-i/2}$ times left multiplication by the rational algebra element $F_i\pi_i$. The latter has a rational minimal polynomial; every complex root occurs in its faithful left regular representation on that ideal. The isometry therefore controls every complex conjugate of $F_i$, not just one chosen embedding. Multiplying back by the positive real number $q^{i/2}$ proves the claimed weights. This supplies the linear algebra of \citet[Lemma 4.6 and Theorem 4.7]{cyKleiman1968}, with the product positivity and algebraic-projector premises visible. Finally the fixed-point formula and the formal identity \[ -\log\det(1-tF_i)=\sum_{m\ge1}\operatorname{Tr}(F_i^m)t^m/m \] give \[ Z(X,t)=\exp\left(\sum_{m\ge1}\#X(\mathbb F_{q^m})\frac{t^m}{m}\right) =\prod_{i=0}^{2n}P_i(t)^{(-1)^{i+1}}. \] Thus the numerator and denominator factors lie in $\mathbb Z[t]$; $P_0(t)=1-t$, $P_{2n}(t)=1-q^nt$, and the zeros of $P_i$ have absolute value $q^{-i/2}$. Poincar\'e duality pairs eigenvalues in complementary degrees by $\alpha\leftrightarrow q^n/\alpha$, yielding \[ Z\left(X,\frac1{q^nt}\right) =\epsilon\,q^{n\chi/2}t^\chi Z(X,t), \qquad \chi=\sum_i(-1)^i\dim H^i(X),\quad \epsilon\in\{1,-1\}. \] More precisely, with $\Delta=\prod_i\det(F_i)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$, the sign is $\epsilon=(-1)^\chi q^{n\chi/2}\Delta$; duality gives $\Delta^2=q^{-n\chi}$. We retain this determinant sign instead of assuming that it is fixed independently of Frobenius. Also $n\chi$ is even: when $n$ is odd, middle Poincar\'e duality is alternating and its dimension is even, while the other terms occur in complementary pairs. Rationality and the functional equation follow formally from the trace formula and duality; the extra standard-conjecture input above supplies the positive-involution proof of the absolute values and semisimplicity. It is not a proof of the general standard conjectures.

Each algebraic class decomposes into algebraic primitive classes: the inverse powers of $L$ needed in the recursive decomposition preserve algebraic classes by $A_H$. Define the usual Lefschetz star by reversing each $L$-string with its Hodge--Riemann sign. It again preserves algebraic classes. Positivity says that, for a nonzero algebraic class $x$, the complementary algebraic class $*x$ satisfies $\deg(x\,*x)>0$. Such an $x$ cannot be numerically zero. Thus homological and numerical equivalence agree under these two hypotheses. This is the mechanism behind the implication $A+H_{\mathrm{std}}\Rightarrow D$; removing algebraicity of the Lefschetz decomposition removes a used premise. Conversely, if $D(X)$ holds in complementary degrees, the numerical pairing identifies the two finite-dimensional numerical cycle spaces as duals. They therefore have the same dimension. Hard Lefschetz injectivity then makes $A_H(X)$ an isomorphism. This argument is about the full numerical pairing, not the asserted positivity of a single primitive middle space.

SA06:C.2e: C.2e (Proved under the stated field-extension hypothesis): $A'_H$ implies $A_H$.. Fix an algebraically closed field $k$ of arbitrary characteristic and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$. We use $\ell$-adic cohomology, with rational cycle coefficients, and write $A^r_H$ for the image of $\mathrm{CH}^r(-)_{\mathbb Q}$ in $H^{2r}(-,\mathbb Q_\ell(r))$. Assume $A'_H$ for all smooth projective varieties and smooth ample hyperplane sections over every algebraically closed extension of $k$. Then $A_H$ holds over all those extensions. In particular the universal implication in the letter is valid. The extension hypothesis is used at the geometric generic fibre of a pencil; we do not replace it by an unsupported assertion about specializing algebraic preimages.

SA06:C.2f: C.2f (Proved): the converse and the exact affine-vanishing gate.. For a smooth ample hyperplane section $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$, $A_H(X)$ already implies $A'_H(X,Y)$. Indeed, for $2r\ge n-1$, write an algebraic class $z\in A_H^{r+1}(X)$ as \[ z=L^{2r+2-n}a,\qquad a\in A_H^{n-r-1}(X), \] using $A_H(X,n-r-1)$. Thus, with the extension-stable universal quantifiers of C.2e, $A_H$ and $A'_H$ are equivalent. Since $A''_H$ is already a theorem by C.2b, the universal implication $A''_H\Rightarrow A'_H$ would prove this standard conjecture $A$; conversely that standard conjecture proves the implication. Together with the product-level equivalences in \citet[Corollary 2.14]{cyKleiman1968}, its exact remaining gate is the universal Lefschetz standard conjecture. SA06:C.1n: C.1n (Proved: the endpoint image criterion is exactly the universal standard conjecture $D$).. We first work over $\mathbb C$ with rational coefficients. Fix integers $n\ge0$ and $0\le r\le n$. Let $\mathcal I_{n,r}$ mean the following assertion: for every smooth projective connected $n$-fold $X$, every smooth projective connected $d$-fold $Y$, every $0\le j\le d$, and every correspondence \[ \Gamma\in\mathrm{CH}^{d+r-j}(Y\times X)_{\mathbb Q}, \] an element $z\in A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ belongs to the image of $\Gamma_*:A^j_{\mathrm{alg}}(Y)\to A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ if and only if its cycle class belongs to the image of \[ \Gamma_*:H^{2j}(Y,\mathbb Q(j)) \longrightarrow H^{2r}(X,\mathbb Q(r)). \] These are the source and degree-shift quantifiers of the image criterion on manuscript page $14{:}46$: its source degree is arbitrary, and the correspondence need not have degree zero. Write $D_{\mathbb C}$ for equality of numerical and Betti homological equivalence on rational cycles of every smooth projective complex variety. Then \begin{equation} \mathcal I_{n,r}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad D_{\mathbb C} \qquad\text{if }r\in\{0,1,n\}. \end{equation} For every $2\le r\le n-1$, the assertion $\mathcal I_{n,r}$ is false by C.1k. If we restrict the target to $X=\mathbb P^n$, its image criterion is equivalent to $D_{\mathbb C}$ for \emph{every} $0\le r\le n$. More precisely, for a \emph{fixed} $X$ and $r$, let $\mathcal I(X,r)$ require the displayed criterion for every source $Y$, source degree $j$, and correspondence $\Gamma$. Then \begin{equation} \mathcal I(X,r)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl(D_{\mathbb C}\ \text{and}\ G^r(X)=0\bigr). \end{equation} \emph{Necessity, including the restricted projective-space target.} Suppose that $D_{\mathbb C}$ fails. Then some smooth projective $d$-fold $Y$ has a numerically trivial rational cycle $a\in\mathrm{CH}^s(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ with $\mathrm{cl}(a)\ne0$. Put $j=d-s$, let $h$ be the hyperplane class on $\mathbb P^n$, and set \[ \Gamma=a\times h^r\in \mathrm{CH}^{s+r}(Y\times\mathbb P^n)_{\mathbb Q}. \] The codimension is $s+r=d+r-j$, as required. The action on cycles is \[ \Gamma_*b=\deg(a\cdot b)h^r=0 \qquad\bigl(b\in A^j_{\mathrm{alg}}(Y)\bigr), \] by numerical triviality. In contrast, Poincar\'e duality supplies $v\in H^{2d-2s}(Y,\mathbb Q(d-s))$ with $\int_Y\mathrm{cl}(a)v=1$. Hence $\Gamma_*v=\mathrm{cl}(h^r)$, although the nonzero cycle class $h^r\in A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(\mathbb P^n)$ is not in the cycle image. This contradicts the proposed criterion. Notice that we neither need nor assert that this cohomological preimage $v$ is algebraic: the criterion itself would force an algebraic preimage, which numerical triviality excludes. The same construction works for any fixed target $X$: take $h$ ample on $X$; its power $h^r$ has nonzero cohomology class, since $\int_Xh^n>0$. Thus $\mathcal I(X,r)$ also implies $D_{\mathbb C}$. Taking $\Gamma=0$ shows separately that $\mathcal I(X,r)$ implies $G^r(X)=0$. \emph{Sufficiency.} Assume $D_{\mathbb C}$. By \citet[Theorem~1, pp.~448--449] {Jannsen1992}, the category of rational numerical motives is semisimple abelian. Betti realization on this category is well defined and faithful: $D_{\mathbb C}$ applies on every product, and K\"unneth together with Poincar\'e duality identifies a correspondence's total cohomology class with its action on all cohomological degrees. Here K\"unneth is only the cohomological decomposition; we do not assume algebraic K\"unneth projectors. We use the convention \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,h(X)(r)) &=A^r_{\mathrm{num}}(X),\\ \operatorname{Hom}(h(Y)(j),h(X)(r)) &=A^{d+r-j}_{\mathrm{num}}(Y\times X). \end{split} \] Thus $\Gamma$ induces a morphism $f:M=h(Y)(j)\to N=h(X)(r)$, and the numerical class of $z$ is a morphism $\beta:\mathbf1\to N$. Semisimplicity gives $g:N\to M$ for which $p=fg$ is a projector onto $\operatorname{im}(f)$ and $pf=f$. If $\mathrm{cl}(z)$ is in the stated cohomological image, then $H((1-p)\beta)=0$. Indeed realization in degree zero of $h(Y)(j)$ and $h(X)(r)$ is precisely the pair of groups in the displayed image criterion. Faithfulness gives $(1-p)\beta=0$, so \[ \beta=f(g\beta). \] Choose a rational cycle $b\in\mathrm{CH}^j(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ representing $g\beta$. We have proved that $\Gamma_*b$ and $z$ are numerically equivalent. In target codimensions $r=0,n$, numerical and algebraic equivalence with rational coefficients are both determined by degree. In codimension $r=1$, the same equality follows from the N\'eron--Severi theorem and the divisor intersection pairing, as recalled in C.1k. Therefore $\Gamma_*b=z$ in $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ in every asserted endpoint case. The converse implication is always given by functoriality of the cycle class. For $X=\mathbb P^n$, the map $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)\to A^r_{\mathrm{num}}(X)$ is an isomorphism in every codimension, so the same proof gives the final restricted-target assertion. For the fixed-target assertion, $D_{\mathbb C}$ identifies numerical and homological equivalence, and $G^r(X)=0$ identifies homological and algebraic equivalence in the specified target group. The same numerical preimage therefore proves \eqref{eq:fixed-target-image-D}. These two equivalences are not restricted to complex geometry. Let $k$ be any algebraically closed field and let $H$ be a fixed Weil cohomology with characteristic-zero coefficient field $F$. Keep rational cycle coefficients, use $F$ in the cohomological image, and define $D_{k,H}$ by equality of numerical and $H$-homological equivalence for rational cycles on every smooth projective $k$-variety. The identical argument proves \[ \mathcal I_{n,r}^{k,H}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ D_{k,H} \qquad(r\in\{0,1,n\}), \] \[ \mathcal I^{k,H}(X,r)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \bigl(D_{k,H}\ \text{and}\ G_H^r(X)=0\bigr), \] where $G_H^r(X)$ is the kernel of the rational-cycle class map into $H^{2r}(X)(r)$. The source functional is evaluated using Poincar\'e duality over $F$; the numerical-motive category and its image splitting still have rational coefficients. Numerical and algebraic equivalence agree rationally for divisors over any algebraically closed field, and degree handles codimensions zero and top. The intermediate-codimension universal counterexamples cited above remain assertions over $\mathbb C$; this extension does not transfer their nonvanishing to positive characteristic. Equations~\eqref{eq:endpoint-image-D}--\eqref{eq:fixed-target-image-D} isolate an exact remaining standard-conjecture gate. It does not prove $D_{\mathbb C}$ and does not replace homological equivalence by algebraic equivalence in intermediate target codimension. The cycle class maps give a commutative diagram with exact rows \[ \begin{array}{ccccccccc} 0&\to&G^r(X)&\to&A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)&\to&A^r_{\mathrm{hom}}(X)&\to&0\\ &&\downarrow L^q&&\downarrow L^q&&\downarrow L^q\\ 0&\to&G^{n-r}(X)&\to&A^{n-r}_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)&\to&A^{n-r}_{\mathrm{hom}}(X)&\to&0. \end{array} \] The last vertical map is injective by hard Lefschetz. The snake lemma therefore gives \[ \begin{split} \ker(L^q|A^r_{\mathrm{alg}})&=\ker(L^q|G^r),\\ 0\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}(L^q|G^r)&\longrightarrow \operatorname{coker}(L^q|A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}) \longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}(L^q|A^r_{\mathrm{hom}}) \longrightarrow0. \end{split} \] Thus the general question contains two separate gates: the Lefschetz map on Griffiths groups, and standard-conjecture surjectivity on algebraic cohomology. SA06:C.3h: C.3h (Known mechanism and proved exact graded gates on abelian varieties).. Let $A$ be a $g$-dimensional abelian variety, $g\ge1$, over an algebraically closed field, of arbitrary characteristic. All groups in this paragraph have rational coefficients. Write \[ B^r(A)=\mathrm{CH}^r(A)_{\mathbb Q}/ \mathrm{CH}^r(A)_{\mathrm{alg},\mathbb Q}, \qquad J^r(A)=\mathrm{CH}^r(A)_{\mathrm{alg},\mathbb Q}. \] Both inherit the Beauville grading, with index $s$ characterized by $[m]^*x=m^{2r-s}x$. In the setting where the ordinary algebraic-equivalence quotient \(B^{N-1}(X)\) is defined, that quotient also vanishes rationally. In particular this gives the ordinary top quotient for the strict-local \(\overline{\mathbb F}_p\)-algebra germs in the manuscript. SA06:C.4c: C.4c (Proved: Question 1 and the generic zero-cycle criterion).. Fix $x_0\in X(k)$, let $A=A_X$, let $a_X:X\to A$ send $x_0$ to $0$, and set $K=k(A)$. Let $\eta_A\in A(K)$ be the generic point. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item There is an integral cycle $\Gamma\in\mathrm{CH}^{n}(A\times X)$ whose action on $H^1$ is inverse to $a_X^*:H^1(A)\to H^1(X)$. \item There is $z\in\mathrm{CH}_0(X_K)^0$ with $\operatorname{alb}_{X_K}(z)=\eta_A$. \end{enumerate} These assertions use one cycle inducing the inverse for all prime-to-characteristic realizations. They are equivalent to existence of a universal zero-cycle, normalized by its fibre over $0$.

SA06:C.4d: C.4d (Proved characterization of Question 2 for abelian varieties).. For an abelian variety $A/k$, Question 2 holds integrally if and only if $A$ is a direct summand, as an unpolarized abelian variety, of a finite product of Jacobians of smooth projective curves. ``Direct summand'' means actual morphisms $s:A\to J$, $r:J\to A$ with $rs=\mathrm{id}_A$, not merely an isogeny decomposition.

SA06:C.4e: C.4e (Proved equivalence for principal polarizations; known counterexamples).. For a principally polarized complex abelian variety $(A,\theta)$ of dimension $g$, Question 2 is equivalent to algebraicity, with \emph{integral} coefficients, of \[ \gamma_\theta=\frac{\theta^{g-1}}{(g-1)!} \in H^{2g-2}(A,\mathbb Z). \] One direction can be read directly from a curve decomposition of $\gamma_\theta$: the induced map $\widehat A\to A$ is the inverse principal polarization, as is checked in a symplectic basis; composing with that polarization gives the identity factorization in C.4d. For the other direction, a direct summand of a product of Jacobians satisfies the integral Hodge conjecture for curves. Indeed the theorem for the product is \citet[Theorem 1.2]{cyBeckmannFortman2023}; pushing an integral Hodge homology class along the inclusion and then pushing an algebraic representative back along the retraction proves the claim for the summand. Apply it to $\gamma_\theta$. This agrees with \citet[Theorem 1.4, Proposition 2.1, Corollary 2.5]{cyVoisin2024}; the published theorem number is 1.4, although an earlier revision labels it 1.3. Over arbitrary algebraically closed fields, the relevant extension is \citet[Theorem 1.2]{cyScaviaSuzuki2025}: it retains the integral $\ell$-adic conditions for every $\ell\ne p$ and the crystalline condition at $p$. Thus a single prime-to-$p$ assertion must not be silently promoted to an integral assertion including $p$. For a principal polarization the polarization itself is already algebraic. Question 2 therefore fails there. Their Corollary 1.2 identifies the cycle-class image in dimensions $4$ and $5$ as exactly $2\mathbb Z\gamma_\theta$. We have checked the theorem and corollary in version 3 of the primary source, and do not substitute a historical claim of openness for this newer result.

Compose it with the integral one-cycle giving the inverse of the Poincar\'e map for $A_X$. The identification $\operatorname{Pic}^0(A_X)\simeq\operatorname{Pic}^0(X)$ identifies the remaining degree-one target. Functoriality of the Poincar\'e bundle makes the composite the inverse of $H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1)\to H^1(B_X)$. SA06:C.4a: C.4a (Proved: degree-one Lefschetz, independent of $\ell$).. Let $X/k$ be smooth projective connected of dimension $n\ge1$, with $k$ algebraically closed. Let $L_1,\ldots,L_{n-1}$ be ample line bundles and $\eta=\prod c_1(L_j)$. For every $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, \begin{equation} \eta\smile-:H^1(X,\mathbb Q_\ell)\xrightarrow{\sim} H^{2n-1}(X,\mathbb Q_\ell)(n-1) \end{equation} has an inverse induced by one rational divisorial correspondence, independent of $\ell$. It is unique as a normalized divisor correspondence class, not as a divisor on $X\times X$.

SA06:C.4b: C.4b (Proved corrected integral form of 2.4--2.5).. Let $X,Y$ be smooth projective connected varieties over $k$ and let $Z\in\mathrm{CH}_1(X\times Y)$ be integral. It defines $u_Z:B_X\to A_Y$ and, for $n=\dim X$, \[ a(Z):H^1(Y,\mathbb Q_\ell)\longrightarrow H^{2n-1}(X,\mathbb Q_\ell)(n-1). \] This is an isomorphism if and only if $u_Z$ is an isogeny. In that case its inverse is induced by the unique class corresponding to $u_Z^{-1}\in\operatorname{Hom}(A_Y,B_X)_{\mathbb Q}$. It is represented by an integral normalized divisor correspondence if and only if $u_Z$ is an isomorphism. More precisely, for a positive integer $m$, \begin{equation} m u_Z^{-1}\in\operatorname{Hom}(A_Y,B_X) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad [m]|_{\ker u_Z}=0 \end{equation} as a morphism of finite group schemes. If the right side holds, $[m]:B_X\to B_X$ factors through the fppf quotient $B_X/\ker u_Z=A_Y$, yielding the left side. Conversely, $(m u_Z^{-1})u_Z=[m]$ kills the kernel. Thus the least positive denominator is the \emph{exponent} of $\ker u_Z$, not generally its order. For $u=[2]$ on a $g$-dimensional abelian variety, it is $2$, whereas the kernel order is $2^{2g}$, including in characteristic $2$ when its scheme structure must be retained. This refutes the strongest literal ``best denominator'' reading of 14:64 while preserving its assertion about the set of possible prime divisors. The induced map \[ H^1(Y,\mathbb Z_\ell)\longrightarrow H^{2n-1}(X,\mathbb Z_\ell)(n-1)/\mathrm{tors} \] is an isomorphism precisely when $u_Z$ is an isogeny of degree prime to $\ell$. Indeed it is the corresponding map of free Tate-module lattices; its index has $\ell$-adic valuation $v_\ell(\deg u_Z)$. An isomorphism before dividing out torsion also requires the target to be torsion free. This is the exact distinction made by the insertions in Corollary 2.5.

SA06:C.4s: C.4s (Known consequence: every supersingular surface is affirmative).. Every supersingular abelian surface over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic is an actual direct summand of a product of Jacobians, including in characteristic two. Indeed, \citet[Lemma 6.2, p.~185]{frC4FuLi2021} prove that it admits a principal polarization. Their Proposition 6.1, p.~184, explicitly includes characteristic two in the N\'eron--Severi lattice calculation used by the proof. The principally polarized surface case C.4f then applies. This does not settle arbitrary nonsupersingular surfaces whose polarization Euler characteristics are all even.

SA06:C.4u: C.4u (Proved: all supersingular threefolds in characteristic at least five).. Every supersingular abelian threefold over an algebraically closed field of characteristic \(p\ge5\) is an actual direct summand of a product of Jacobians. In characteristics two and three we obtain, respectively, \[ s_J(A)\mid2\quad(p=2),\qquad s_J(A)\mid3\quad(p=3); \] these two divisibilities do not by themselves prove a retraction. More generally, for a supersingular abelian variety \(A\) of dimension \(g\ge1\), \begin{equation} s_J(A)\mid p^{\,v_p((2g-1)!)}. \end{equation} In particular every such \(A\) is a direct summand if \(p>2g-1\).

SA06:C.4v: C.4v (Proved: full real multiplication removes every polarization gcd obstruction in characteristic zero).. Let \(A\) be an abelian variety of dimension \(g\) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Suppose that there is an action \[ \mathcal O_F\hookrightarrow\operatorname{End}(A) \] of the full ring of integers of a totally real field \(F\) of degree \(g\), and a polarization whose Rosati involution fixes \(F\) pointwise. Then \[ \delta(A)=1. \] In particular, if \(g\le3\), \(A\) is an actual direct summand of a product of Jacobians. This includes a simple abelian surface or threefold with \(\operatorname{End}(A)=\mathcal O_K\) for a CM field \(K\) of degree \(2g\). No principal polarization on \(A\) is assumed. There is a useful local refinement. Suppose an order \(\mathcal O\subset F\), rather than the full integer ring, acts with the same Rosati property, and put \(c=[\mathcal O_F:\mathcal O]\). Then every prime divisor of \(\delta(A)\) divides \(c\). Consequently an abelian surface with \(c\) odd, or an abelian threefold with \(\gcd(c,6)=1\), is still an actual direct summand of a product of Jacobians. These conclusions require local maximality only at two, or at two and three, respectively.

SA06:C.4w: C.4w (Proved: ordinary full-real-multiplication varieties in every characteristic).. Let \(k\) be algebraically closed of characteristic \(p>0\), including \(p=2\), and let \(A/k\) be ordinary of dimension \(g\). Suppose that the full ring of integers of a totally real field \(F\) of degree \(g\) acts on \(A\), and that a polarization has Rosati involution fixing \(F\) pointwise. Then \(\delta(A)=1\). In dimensions at most three, \(A\) is therefore an actual direct summand of a product of Jacobians. More generally, if an order \(\mathcal O\subset F\) acts with the same Rosati property, every prime divisor of \(\delta(A)\) divides \([\mathcal O_F:\mathcal O]\). Hence odd index suffices for an ordinary surface, and index prime to six suffices for an ordinary threefold, including in characteristics two and three.

SA06:C.4x: C.4x (Proved: full real multiplication in arbitrary positive characteristic).. Let \(k\) be algebraically closed of characteristic \(p>0\), and let \(A/k\) have dimension \(g\). Suppose that the full integer ring of a totally real field of degree \(g\) acts: \[ \mathcal O_F\hookrightarrow\operatorname{End}(A), \qquad [F:\mathbb Q]=g. \] We assume that \(A\) has a polarization whose Rosati involution fixes \(F\) pointwise, equivalently an \(\mathcal O_F\)-linear polarization. Then the integer \(\delta(A)\) of C.4j is a power of \(p\), with exponent possibly zero. If, in addition, \begin{equation} [\operatorname{Lie}(A)] =[\mathcal O_F\otimes_{\mathbb Z} k] \quad\text{in }G_0(\mathcal O_F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}k), \end{equation} where \(G_0\) is the Grothendieck group of finite modules, then \[ \delta(A)=1. \] Condition \eqref{eq:c4-hb-lie-condition} is automatic if \(p\) is totally ramified in \(F\). There is no ordinarity or supersingularity hypothesis, and \(p=2\) and \(p=3\) are included. Consequently, in dimensions two and three respectively, \begin{equation} s_J(A)\mid p^{v_p(2)} \quad(g=2),\qquad s_J(A)\mid p^{v_p(6)} \quad(g=3). \end{equation} Every such surface in characteristic different from two, and every such threefold in characteristic at least five, is an actual direct summand of a product of Jacobians. In every characteristic, including the remaining two small primes, \eqref{eq:c4-hb-lie-condition} gives the same affirmative conclusion for \(g\le3\). In particular this holds when the characteristic is totally ramified in the acting real field.
